concerns.text: T022 instructs to 'shuffle labels independently within each outer fold iteration' for the permutation test. This violates the data-flow dependency on the Plan/Spec which mandates a GLOBAL permutation (shuffling Y once before the outer loop) to establish a valid null hypothesis. The consumer (T022) is implementing a logic that contradicts the producer (Plan.md/FR-004) definition of the null distribution, rendering the statistical artifact invalid.

T032 implements sensitivity analysis by splitting participants based on 'predicted values' (model output). This violates the dependency on the Spec (FR-007) which requires a sweep of the 'median-split threshold' on the *observed* heat-pain threshold labels (ground truth). The task consumes the wrong artifact (predictions) to perform a robustness check on the ground truth definition, breaking the intended statistical flow.

T008 (DataLoader) includes a rhetorical question ('How can we optimize feature aggregation...') and a placeholder claim. This is not a concrete task definition. A task that emits an artifact (the loader) must have a deterministic description. The presence of unresolved claims and questions prevents the task from being a valid producer for downstream consumers (T012-T017).

T022 references '[deferred]' iterations for the permutation test. The Spec (FR-004) explicitly mandates '1,000 permutations'. A task consuming the Spec requirement cannot defer the core parameter of the statistical test. This creates a missing dependency for the permutation logic, making the task non-executable as defined.

T011 includes an unresolved claim marker '[UNRESOLVED-CLAIM: c_04d00f08...]' inside the task description text. While not a hard ordering violation, task descriptions must be self-contained and executable. Embedding unresolved claims in the task body obscures the acceptance criteria for the consumer (the test runner).
